Characteristic APL blasts showing densely packed cytoplasm with large granules and bundles of Auer rods (Giemsa) (<<30889>>). Bone marrow smear of an APL promyelocyte representing the microgranular form of APL (variant) (<<40736>>).

Translocation results from the breakage and rejoining of bands 15q24 and 17q21. G-banded normal chromosomes 15 and 17 are shown on the outside of each pair of homologues, and the points of rearrangement on each derivative chromosome 15 and 17 from the translocation are indicated by arrows.

Dual-colour dual-fusion FISH strategy with probes for PML (15q24.1) and RARA (17q21.2). Representative interphase nucleus with abnormal PML::RARA dual-fusion signal pattern (arrow): one normal PML signal (red), one normal RARA signal (green), and two PML::RARA fusion signals indicating the 15;17 translocation; a normal nucleus is also present (two red signals for normal PML and two green signals for normal RARA) (<<40770>>). Representative interphase nucleus with an atypical pattern of three RARA signals and no PML::RARA rearrangement (arrows): two normal PML signals (red) and three RARA signals (green), which may indicate gain of RARA at 17q21.2 or rearrangement of RARA with a partner other than PML; a normal nucleus is also present (two red signals for normal PML and two green signals for normal RARA); images of individual nuclei were merged from the same case (<<40769>>). Break-apart probe strategy for RARA (17q21.2) showing representative interphase nuclei with abnormal RARA rearrangement signal pattern (arrows): one normal intact fusion signal and separated red 5′ RARA and green 3′ RARA signals; this confirms that the pattern of three RARA signals shown in Fig. <<40769>> represents one normal RARA signal and one RARA rearrangement with a partner other than PML; a normal nucleus is also present (two intact fusion signals). Confirming RARA rearrangement has implications for the potential treatment response, which may vary depending on the partner gene (<<40768>>).
